material_facts.statement: ICRA reaffirmed Indoco's long-term ratings at [ICRA]A with a Negative outlook and short-term ratings at [ICRA]A2+ on Rs 1,019.65 crore of facilities (30 September 2026).
Rated facilities comprise Rs 400.00 crore term loans, Rs 94.40 crore cash credit and Rs 335.00 crore short-term fund-based limits among others.
The Negative outlook reflects elevated debt, weak debt-protection metrics and moderately high working capital intensity despite recovery in FY2026 operations.
Consolidated revenue grew 10.8% to Rs 1,845.3 crore in FY2026.
Export formulation revenues grew 28.7% in FY2026, with regulated markets up 14.4% and non-regulated markets up 65.5%.
USFDA permitted restart of two of four production lines at Goa Plant II by July 2025 after the lines were shut in April 2024.
Goa Plants II and III received OAI status in June 2023 and a USFDA warning letter followed the February 2024 re-audit.
A USFDA reinspection of Goa Plant II on 27 August to 4 September 2026 resulted in seven Form 483 observations.
Operating margin improved to 7.7% in FY2026 from 6.0% in FY2025 and to 8.8% in Q1 FY2027 from 4.0%.
Q1 FY2027 operating income rose 6.0% year on year to Rs 467.5 crore.
Net loss widened to Rs 98.7 crore in FY2026 from Rs 78.0 crore in FY2025 because of higher depreciation and finance costs.
Total debt was Rs 1,084.2 crore at 31 March 2026 and total debt to OPBDITA was 7.6 times.
Interest coverage was 1.2 times and DSCR 0.7 times in FY2026.
Working capital intensity was 34.6% in FY2026 against 37.7% in FY2025.
Inventory days fell to 124 from 139, while creditor days rose to 198 from 141 amid cash-flow pressure.
Liquidity is adequate: free cash and liquid investments were Rs 26.2 crore and average working capital utilisation was 90.7% over 12 months to July 2026.
Debt servicing obligations are Rs 145.8 crore for FY2027 and Rs 145.3 crore for FY2028.
Indoco received about Rs 100 crore from monetising its ophthalmic business and about Rs 64 crore from a Mumbai land sale in H1 FY2027.
Warren Remedies (OTC oral care subsidiary) revenue rose about 34% to Rs 120.6 crore in FY2026 but its loss before tax widened to Rs 64.3 crore from Rs 36.0 crore.
Domestic and export formulations contributed 46.6% and 36.8% of FY2026 revenues respectively.
About 11% to 13% of domestic formulations are under NLEM price controls.
Rating downgrade triggers include inability to scale additional capacities and delays in resolving regulatory non-compliance.
The rating history shows downgrades from AA- (Negative) to A (Negative) between January and August 2025.
Consolidated income from operations was Rs 1,845.32 crore in FY2026 against Rs 1,664.92 crore in FY2025.
Consolidated net profit after tax was a loss of Rs 98.67 crore in FY2026 against a loss of Rs 77.95 crore in FY2025.
Consolidated finance cost rose to Rs 122.25 crore from Rs 66.23 crore, and depreciation to Rs 126.45 crore from Rs 113.84 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA (profit before finance cost, depreciation and tax) was Rs 145.16 crore against Rs 104.71 crore.
The board recommended a dividend of Rs 0.20 per equity share of Rs 2, the same as the previous year.

The auditors' report includes an Emphasis of Matter on going-concern uncertainty at an investee (FPP Holding LLC) with a net loss of Rs 2,365.21 lakh and negative net worth of Rs 4,225.11 lakh; the opinion is not modified.
The company reports it has not defaulted in repayment of dues or other borrowings or interest to any lender (CARO statement).
